context: Resolve GATES or STAGED_GATES in _bounded_value_gate_scale, matching oracle_surface_provenance. Validate gate.surface_independence against a closed _KNOWN_PROVENANCE_LABELS set and raise with an actionable message naming both edits a new label needs. description: generate_oracle_coverage_map.py has two holes in how it reads live cross-surface gate metadata. (1) _bounded_value_gate_scale() resolves only GATES, but classify_oracles() already treats a STAGED gate as a cross-surface oracle, so a staged gate declaring its own scale_factor renders the shared EQUIVALENCE_SCALE instead -- overstating the scale at which the gate holds, on the exact path every gate takes before promotion. oracle_surface_provenance() twelve lines away already resolves GATES or STAGED_GATES, so the two are inconsistent. Reproduced by staging a probe gate with scale_factor=0.001: the row rendered SF=0.1. (2) The provenance label is returned straight from gate.surface_independence with no vocabulary check. The tests pin the three PROVENANCE_* constants to the live SURFACE_INDEPENDENCE_* constants, which catches a RENAME but not an ADDITION, so a newly registered gate carrying a new label renders into the table while the map's own Surface-provenance prose still defines only three -- legend contradicting row. Reproduced by adding SURFACE_INDEPENDENCE_TRANSPILED: it rendered silently. Both latent today (STAGED_GATES is empty) and neither changes the committed artifact.
